thread:
support-ops: URGENT: Acme PROD private peering — customers reporting intermittent 502/504s and TLS handshake failures to our private control-plane after they applied a vendor ACL change this morning. Escalating to SRE + Infra. :rotating_light:

sre-elena: Oncall here. Are they running IPsec or a DX link? Any BGP flaps?

support-ops: They are on IPsec (strongSwan) with two tunnels. BGP shows ESTABLISHED on both peers but app traffic times out intermittently. Also seeing DNS for cp FQDN sometimes NXDOMAIN, sometimes resolves.

eng-infra-raj: Can we get `ipsec statusall`, a short `tcpdump` of SYNs to the control-plane IP, and an `openssl s_client -connect` from a host behind their FW? Also: what control-plane CIDRs are in their egress allowlist?

support-ops: Pasting redacted snippets they shared:
```
# ipsec statusall
IKEv2 SAs:
  peer[1] INSTALLED, IKE SA up
  peer[2] REKEYING, retransmit count high
CHILD_SA acme->redwood{1}: INSTALLED
CHILD_SA acme->redwood{2}: rekeying, PACKET_LOSS

# tcpdump (filtered)
12:03:11.123 IP acme-host > cp-ip: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1400], length 0
12:03:11.456 IP cp-ip > acme-host: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
12:03:12.000 IP acme-host > cp-ip: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1400], length 0
# repeated retransmits, occasional ICMP 'Fragmentation needed' seen
```

support-ops: openssl from behind their proxy to `cp1.redwood-private.net:443`:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect cp1.redwood-private.net:443 -servername cp1.redwood-private.net
CONNECTED(00000003)
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
No peer certificate available
---
SSL handshake failure
```

eng-infra-raj: Two likely signals: 1) MSS/DF/MTU path issue — mss 1400 + ICMP frag suggests PMTUD broken or DF set on tunnel. 2) "No peer certificate" points to TLS interception or an intermediate proxy replying instead of our control-plane. Do they use a corporate TLS inspection appliance? Also check if their allowlist contains the correct control-plane CIDRs (stale IPs are common).

security-ops: Indeed many enterprise proxies terminate TLS and re-issue a cert; that will break mTLS and cert verification. Ask them whether the appliance is set to intercept egress to external hosts and whether SNI is preserved/passthrough is possible.

customer-success-liz: I'm on a call with Acme infra. They confirmed they pushed a vendor ACL that funnels egress through a corporate proxy/inspection appliance. They also enabled DF on the tunnel and have an MTU clamp at 1420 on the FW. They admit the allowlist had an old /24 for our control plane.

eng-ml-omar: Adds that model fetches were failing with 403s earlier — consistent with a proxy re-signing TLS and invalidating signed S3/GCS requests (signatures no longer match).

sre-elena: Workarounds to propose to customer now:
- Whitelist our control-plane CIDRs by IP and allow raw TCP/TLS passthrough (no termination).
- If proxy cannot be disabled, configure it to preserve SNI and not terminate mTLS for our endpoints.
- As a short-term network fix, relax DF or enable MSS clamping to a lower value (e.g., 1360) to avoid fragmentation failures.

support-ops: Acme tried FQDN whitelisting but the proxy rewrites SNI. They prefer IP allowlists. We gave them our current control-plane prefixes: `54.23.12.0/24` and `34.56.78.0/24` (redacted). They had `54.23.9.0/24` still pinned; they updated the allowlist during the call.

eng-infra-raj: Also confirm NAT-T/UDP 4500 is allowed end-to-end. If the proxy/NAT changes source ports, NAT-T handling can disrupt child SA/auth.

vendor-fw: Vendor rep on the bridge says they can disable TLS inspection for those CIDRs and will loosen the DF policy on the tunnel. They'll also enable MSS clamp to 1360 on egress for the impacted flows. Changes expected to propagate in ~8-12 minutes.

oncall-bot: Incident created: severity=P1 — paging oncall rotation and opening conference bridge.

sre-elena: After the vendor applied changes we observed successful TLS handshakes and the client presented its cert to the control-plane (mTLS visible). tcpdump no longer shows ICMP fragmentation messages.

customer-success-liz: Acme reports API latencies returned to normal and model downloads resumed. They saw transient 502s during the change window but now stable. They temporarily rolled back the corporate ACL to expedite recovery.

support-ops: Preliminary root cause: corporate proxy/TLS inspection + stale control-plane CIDR in customer allowlist + DF/MTU mismatch produced intermittent fragmentation and TLS handshake failures (proxy responded instead of control-plane -> no peer cert). Remediation we recommended: whitelist by CIDR and allow TLS passthrough for Redwood endpoints, or configure proxy to preserve SNI and not terminate mTLS; enable MSS clamp or allow PMTUD; ensure UDP 4500 and NAT-T pass-through.

security-ops: We'll add explicit guidance to the enterprise onboarding checklist: require customers to allow TLS passthrough and preserve SNI for Private deployments, and to verify control-plane CIDRs on any egress ACL.

support-ops: Closing thread — Acme stable. We'll open a formal postmortem and update runbooks in ~24h. :white_check_mark:
